value_proposition.explanation: Across both sources, the useful lifestyle value is mobile professional work moving from ideas to meetings, review, collaboration, and decisions across offices, home, and shared spaces. Final prompts express that through ordinary desks, notebooks, sketchbooks, papers, pens, and warm workplace or residential settings without depicting the product itself.

debug.input_assessment: Both documents describe the same product and broadly consistent audience: mobile executives, hybrid knowledge workers, enterprise teams, and distributed work across offices, home, client sites, and shared spaces. The most usable scene cues are office, home workspace, shared-space work, sketching, presenting, review, meetings, collaboration, sensitive work, and content creation. Technical claims were treated as non-visual unless they naturally supported a work context.
debug.count_explanation: Generated exactly 20 distinct prompts. The set includes Home, Office, Education, Gaming, Café, and Creative Studio, with source-first sorting by source_relevance_score and then C-Tech reference proximity.
ignored_fields: Transport/run metadata such as Run, Status, Created, Exported, and Model.
Authoring directions, claims validation instructions, disclaimers, SEO rank data, and competitor search URLs that do not provide ordinary scene evidence.
Device-specific appearance, brand, model, ports, screen, and mode descriptions in final prompt text.
debug.diversity_summary: The bank varies ordinary C-Tech settings across corporate office tables, home workspaces, living-room surfaces, creative offices, neighborhood café tables, classroom/library study tables, and gaming rooms. Diversity comes from reference-led changes in setting and object clusters, not invented specialty counters or unsupported workflows.
limitations: The camera profile is wide and oblique with up to three local props and two background details, so some rich C-Tech room inventories were reduced.
Education and Gaming are required coverage categories but are not supported by the source documents; they are marked as creative departures with low source relevance.
Café is treated as adjacent to supported shared spaces, not as an explicitly sourced setting.
No people were added because the references do not need them and the sources can be expressed through objects and settings.
No target device or extra computing hardware is described in prompt text.
